2027 TENTATIVE OPERATING BUDGE]
September 30, 2026
Dear Town Clerk and Members of the Town Board:
As Supervisor and Chief Fiscal Officer of the Town of Brookhaven, and in accordance with Section 106
of New York State Town Law, I am pleased to present the 2027 Tentative Operating Budget for your
consideration.
This ts my third budget as Supervisor, and i reflects the pnnciples that continue to guide my
administration: protect taxpayers, maintain strong Town services, invest in our communities and
plan responsibly for Brookhaven’s future,
The 2027 Tentative Operating Budget is structurally balanced across all six major tax districts without
using fund balance to support operations. [i remains well below the New York State Property Tax Levy
Cap, with a 1.70% adjustment after accounting for the new LIPA PILOT agreement reflected in 2026
property taxes.
These results are nol achieved by chance. Thev are the product of conservative budgeting, long-term
planning and a disciplined approach to how taxpayer dollars are spent.
Brookhaven’s financial strength continues to receive independent recognition. In 2026, both Moody's
Ratings and S&P Global Ratings reaffirmed the Town at AAA/‘Aaa—the highest credit ratings
avVailable—with stable outlooks. The New York State Comptroller has also reported a 0.0 Fiscal Stress
Score for Brookhaven, the best possible score and another independent measure of lhe Town's strong
financial condition.
Those results are important because fiscal responsibility is not simply about numbers on a page. Strong
finances allow us to maintain services, invest in infrastructure and parks, preserve open space, respond to
emergencies and plan for the future while protecting the taxpayers who ultimately pay the bills.
Confronting Rising Costs with Transparency
Like municipalities across Long Island, Brookhaven continues to face financial pressures that originate
bevond Town Hall. State-mandated pension contributions, mereasing health imsurance expenses and the
changing economics of solid-waste management continue to place pressure on local budgets.
We cannot control every outside cos! imposed upon the Town. We can control how honestly and
transparently we account for those costs.
i

3.text:
For that reason, this budget provides residents with a clear accounting of the actual costs associated with
residential refuse and recycling collection and disposal. These expenses are identified through a dollar-
for-dollar user fee so residents can see what these services cost and track those costs from year to vear.
For atypical single-family home, the 2027 Garbage and Refuse User Fee is limited to a 1.5% adjustment,
bringing the total to S395, 52.
This is about transparency. Residents deserve to know where their money goes, what services actually
cost and why those costs change.
Focusing Town Government on Its Core Responsibilities
This budget also continues my effort to focus Town resources on the fundamental responsibilities of local
government and to make Brookhaven more responsive to the people we serve.
Our Town faces two challenges that must be addressed together: providing appropnale opportunities for
housing and economic redevelopment while continuing our aggressive efforts to preserve open space and
protect our environment.
Across Brookhaven, community-supported redevelopment plans are creating opportunities for housing,
economic activity and the revitalization of existing commercial areas. Al the same time, we continue to
fund open-space acquisition and environmental preservation.
We are also working to make Town government faster and easier to navigate.
We have eliminated unnecessary boards and redirected resources toward professional staff, including a
new Chief Building Inspector charged with improving management, creating efficiencies and streamlining
the application and permitting process.
The objective is simple: less unnecessary bureaucracy, better customer service and greater
accountability.
Investing in the People Who Protect Brookhaven’s Quality of Life
A fiscally responsible government must control spending, but it must also recognize where investment 1s
necessary. For that reason, the 2027 budget continues to invest in the Town employees who perform the
essential work that residents expect from their local government every day.
From maintaining our parks and public facilities to protecting our environment, responding to constituent
concems, enforcing our codes and ensuring the safety and integnty of our neighborhoods, our employees
are on the front lines of maintaining the quality of life that makes Brookhaven a desirable place to
live, work and raise a family.
That commitment is particularly important when it comes to code enforcement and our continuing
crackdown on illegal housing.

ij

4.text:
[legal housing 1s nol simply a zoning issue. [It can create serious public safety concems, place additional
burdens on neighborhoods and infrastructure, negatively affect surrounding properties and undermine the
quality of life of residents who follow the law.
That is why we will continue to dedicate the personnel and resources necessary lo aggressively
investigate illegal housing, enforce the Town Code and hold property owners accountable when they
disregard our laws.
At the same time, we are investing in the professional staff necessary to make the legitimate building and
permitting process more efficient and accessible. Residents and businesses who follow the rules should
receive timely, professional service, while those who intentionally violate our codes should expect
meaningful enforcement.
Efficiency and enforcement go hand in hand, We can make Town government easier to navigate for
those doing the right thing while being more effective in addressing those who are not.
These are investments in people, but more importantly, they are investments in Brookhaven's
neighborhoods, public safety and quality of life.
Keeping Brookhaven’s Share of the Tax Bill Low
li is also important for residents to understand where the Town fits within their overall property tax bill.
In 2026, the Town's share represented approximately 7.51% of the total local property tax bill for
properties outside incorporated villages and approximately 4.0% within village areas, based upon
the 2025-2026 Property Tax Warrant certified by the Suffolk County Legislature. We anticipate that
Brookhaven Town government will continue to represent a similarly small portion of the overall property
tax bill in 2027.
Our responsibility is to make every one of those taxpayer dollars count.
2027 Tentative Operating Budget Highlights
* Stays below the New York State Property Tax Levy Cap. at 1.70% after the LIPA PILOT
adjustment;
* Uses no fund balance to balance the six major tax districts:
* Maintains compliance with the Town's local tax-rate and debt-management caps:
® Supports Grookhaven’s AAA/Aaa eredit ratings from S&P Global and Moody's:
® Priorilizes spending on the core functions of Town government and the employees who deliver
essential services:
« (Continues the Town's aggressive enforcement against illegal housing and serious code
violations,
* Reduces property taxes across the Town's nine Ambulance Districts by 2.05%:
* Fully funds our commitment to parks and open-space acquisition:
® Limits the Garbage and Refuse User Fee adjustment for a typical single-family home to 1.5%, or
S$395.52; and
* Adds another $200,000 to the Land fill Post-Closure Reserve, bringing the anticipated reserve to
approximately S30 million,
iti

5.text:
This budget demonstrates that fiscal discipline and investment in our communities are not competing
fouls, We can—and must—do both.
Brookhaven enters 2027 with structurally balanced major funds, the hizhest possible credit ratings, strong
reserves and a continuing commitment to responsible long-term financial planning. At the same time, we
are investing in the employees who maintain our parks, protect our environment, enforce our codes and
serve our residents; preserving open space, supporting emergency medical services; and improving the
way residents interact with Town government.
There will always be pressures on local government and difficult decisions to make. Our obligation is to
confront those challenges directly, spend responsibly, enforce our laws fairly, remain transparent with the
public and protect the quality of life that Brookhaven residents expect and deserve.
look forward to working with my colleagues on the Town Board and with our residents over the coming
month as the 2027 Operating Budget process continues,
Sincerely,
eg

——
Daniel J. Panico
Supervisor
Town of Brookhaven

OFFICE OF THE TOWN COUNCIL
Mission Statement:
The mission of the Town Council Office is to establish sound public policy, enact
legislation and take appropriate action to address the needs and priorities of
Brookhaven residents. The Town Council is committed to representing the public
interest, providing responsible oversight of municipal operations, and planning for the
Town's future while maintaining responsive and effective local government.
Department Description
The Brookhaven Town Council consists of six members, each elected to serve a four-
year term. The Town is geographically divided into six council districts, providing
residents with direct representation in Town government.
Council district boundaries are periodically reviewed and revised in accordance with
federal and state requirements following the decennial U.S. Census. Most recently, the
District Maps were revised on September 29, 2022, based upon the result of the 2020
U.S. Census.
Council members are responsible for establishing Town policy, amending the Town
Code, adopting local laws, and establishing policies and procedures governing Town
operations. The Town Council also reviews and approves the Town's annual Operating
and Capital Budgets, helping to establish financial priorities and ensure the responsible
allocation of Town resources.
11

22.text:
In addition to their legislative responsibilities, the Town Council Offices serve as an
important connection between residents and Town government. Council Offices address
constituent concerns, respond to resident inquiries, coordinate with Town
departments, and assist in resolving complaints and other matters affecting their
respective districts. These efforts help ensure that residents receive timely, fair,
and responsive assistance from Town government.

27.text:
OFFICE OF THE SUPERVISOR
Mission Statement:
To provide effective leadership and oversight of Town government, responsibly manage
the Town's finances and day-to-day operations, and ensure the efficient delivery of
services that support the safety and welfare of Brookhaven residents.
Department Description
The Office of the Supervisor provides executive leadership and oversight of the day-to-
day operations of Town government. As the Town's Chief Fiscal Officer, the Supervisor
is responsible for maintaining a balanced budget, promoting sound fiscal management
and supporting the Town's long-term financial stability.
The Office coordinates with Town departments and divisions, prepares agendas for
Town Board meetings, responds to résident inquiries, and manages scheduling,
communications and special projects on behalf of the Supervisor.
The Office of the Supervisor includes the Call Center, Division of Personnel, Division of
Public Information and Board of Ethics.
Call Center - The Call Center operates 451-TOWN, the Town of Brookhaven’s
Constituent Response Center, providing residents with a central point of contact for
Town information and services. Call Center representatives respond to general inquiries
and assist residents with requests involving garbage collection and recycling, public
safety, code enforcement, street lighting, highway maintenance, parks, Town events
and other municipal services. Through 451-TOWN, residents have one convenient
telephone number to access information and services across Town government.
Personnel - The Division of Personnel oversees employment opportunities, recruitment
and human resources services for the Town of Brookhaven, supporting the Town's full-
time, part-time and seasonal workforce. The Division works with the Suffolk County
Department of Civil Service to administer hiring and employment processes and is
responsible for personnel functions including Civil Service compliance, labor relations,
benefits administration, employee programs and services, and coordination of payroll-
related functions with the Department of Finance. The Division also promotes equal
employment opportunities and a fair and inclusive workplace.
Public Information - The Division of Public Information manages the dissemination of
important Town government information to residents, employees and the media
through press releases, publications, advertisements, special events, the Town website,
social media and other communication platforms. The Division also serves as a primary
source of public communication during Town emergencies and other significant events.
1F

28.text:
Public Information manages the content and maintenance of the Town's official website
and produces video programming and informational content, including Brookhaven
Today and Supervisor Panico on the Air. The Division oversees government access
Channel 18, the Town's television studio and related audio/video equipment, and
coordinates the recording and broadcasting of Town Board and other public meetings,
Town Board presentations, special events, public service announcements and other
Town programming.

Board of Ethics - The Board of Ethics is a nonpartisan body responsible for interpreting
and administering the Town's ethics statutes and helping Town officials and employees
understand and avoid potential conflicts of interest. The Board reviews written requests
for ethics opinions, provides guidance on matters involving ethical standards and
conduct, and works to promote the highest standards of integrity in Town government
while maintaining the confidentiality required for matters before the Board.

45.text:
OFFICE OF THE ASSESSOR
Mission Statement:
The mission of the Town of Brookhaven Assessor's Office is to provide outstanding
service to our residents, fairly administer the real property tax exemption process and
maintain the physical information to fairly and equitably value all real property within
the Town. The Department seeks to create an equitable annual assessment roll that is
at a uniform percentage of market value, as required by New York State Real Property
Tax Law, and provide residents with any information necessary to review the accuracy
of their property's assessed value.
Assessor's Office Description
The Assessor is appointed by the Town Board for a six-year term of office. The
responsibilities of the office are governed by operation of the New York State Real
Property Tax Law. The Assessor is responsible for estimating the assessed value of all
property within the Town. Each assessment must be equitable with respect to other
similarly situated properties and at a uniform percentage of the properties’ market
Value.
New York State law authorizes the Assessor to grant certain real property tax
exemptions to property owners and specific types of properties. The exemption process
requires the annual review of each application and supporting documentation to
determine eligibility.
The Assessor's Office performs the following tasks:
Valuation - Estimates the value of residential and commercial property, reviews
existing assessments for fairness and equity.
Exemptions - Advises the Supervisor and Town Board of changes to State Law that
impact the amount and type of real property tax exemptions granted by the Assessor.
Drafting - Assists the Suffolk County Real Property Tax Service Agency with maintaining
the Town tax maps and resolves title and legal issues of property throughout the Town.
Oata Entry and Record Storage - Maintains the physical information about each property
within the Town.
Public Information - Provides real property tax exemption applications to the public
and access to public assessment records.
a5

46.text:
Production of Certificate of Assessment _& Rodius Maps: Provides Certificate of
Assessments and Radius Maps both in person and virtually. The radius maps are used by
the Planning Board and the Zoning Board of Appeals to assist applications to notify
interested parties of the pending hearing dates. This is currently done from a separate
counter, exclusively devoted to providing this service to constituents both in person
and online.

Assessor's Office Accomplishments for 2026

« Adopted and implemented the new exemption eligibility legislation prescribed
by New York State,

=» Began transitioning to the new Infor system, resulting in a more streamlined and
efficient FOIL (Freedom of Information Law) processing workflow.

» Continually update the Assessor’s webpage to provide the most up-to-date
information for the public.

® Began an initiative to work more closely with local school districts to ensure
SCAR petitions are valid and properly filed, recognizing that SCAR applicants
must submit petitions to both the Town and the school district. This
collaboration helps maintain accuracy, prevent improper filings, and support a
more consistent review process.

* Further strengthened and refined departmental policies and procedures to
ensure the Town's Assessment Roll is thoroughly protected and effectively
supported throughout Tax Certiorari and Small Claims Assessment Review
proceedings.

« Further enhanced the electronic filing system for grievances and conducted the
Assessor's Grievance Day in person, as well as adding a second in person day to
support influx.

« Continued full compliance with New York State’s mandate for secondary
senior-citizen exemption notification, delivering information to Brookhaven
residents in a more streamlined and cost-effective manner.

« Continued reviewing all exemptions that no longer apply to specific parcels to
ensure accuracy and support increases to the taxable assessment roll.

Assessor's Office Goals for 2027

* Continually update the Assessor's Office webpage to provide more detailed
assessment roll information and specific property inventory information.

* Work to get Assessor's Office staff fully trained and up to speed with the new
Infor system, improving integration and communication with other Town
departments such as Building, Planning, Information Technology, and Law.

DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE
Mission Statement:
To oversee the Town of Brookhaven'’s Purchasing, Accounting, Debt Management,
Grants, Insurance and Risk Management, Cash Investments, Ambulance Financial
Coordination, and Budgetary preparation compliance functions. The Department
ensures compliance with all applicable New York State laws, Comptroller requirements,
local laws, Generally Accepted Government Accounting Standards, federal statutes,
and Town Board policies.
D             D     te
The Finance Department manages the Town's day-to-day fiscal operations, including
recording transactions, issuing financial reports, managing cash flow, investments, billing,
accounts receivable, and revenue accounting, It oversees purchasing activities, vendor
management, purchase orders, invoice processing, payments, payroll administration, and
internal controls.
The Department manages Public Improvement and Capital Project finances, including debt
issuance and maintenance of credit-rating agency relationships. It oversees Risk
Management, Insurance Policies, Internal Audit, the annual external audit, and preparation
of audited financial statements.
The Department administers the application, award, and reimbursement of Grants and
prepares the annual Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (SEF A).
The Purchasing Division administers the Town's Procurement Policy and issues public bids and
requests for proposals, ensuring objective competition, preventing waste and favoritism, and
protecting taxpayers’ interests. All procurement activities comply with federal, state,
county, and local regulations.
The Department supports development of the annual operating and capital budgets, provides
budget oversight and compliance throughout the fiscal year, and issues required financial
and budgetary reports.

DEPARTMENT OF GENERAL SERVICES
Mission Statement:
The Department of General Services strives to provide support services to enable Town
Departments to meet their goals in best servicing the residents of the Town of Brookhaven
through a variety of Divisions, ranging from the Vehicle Control Division for vehicle
procurement, replacement and efficient feet management, management of pool
vehicles, a tank compliance program, and fuel site management; Central Reproduction
and Mailroom Divisions for in-house copy reproduction and mail distribution, and Space
Management support services. Additionally, the General Services Department includes
the Abandoned Vehicles & Impounds Division, the Office of the Town Historian, and the
four Human Services Divisions, providing programs and resources to aid and support
Youth, Seniors, Veterans and Women’s Services within the community.
D        !        1D       oti
The Department of General Services is responsible for the management of the Central
Motor Pool, Vehicle Control, Impounds and Abandoned Vehicles Divisions, Central
Reproduction and Mailing Divisions, Space Management, Office of the Town Historian,
as well as providing vital programs through its Human Services Divisions, which include
the Youth Bureau, Senior Citizens Division and Nutrition Program, Veterans Services
Division, Women's Services Division, and Dress for Success Brookhaven.
Division of Space Management- The Division of Space Management's function is to meet
operational needs in terms of productive use of space and finances. Collaboration to
meet the overall missions of various departments as well as individual needs is
necessary to deliver services effectively and efficiently. Requests from outside
organizations for use of space inside and outside of Town Hall are also managed by the
Department of General Services.
Division of Vehicle Contro!- The Division of Vehicle Control is responsible for ordering,
maintaining and final disposition of the Town's fleet of vehicles. The auto mechanics
at Vehicle Control provide repair, service and maintenance to over 350 town- owned
vehicles, heavy-duty equipment and machinery. Vehicles deemed surplus are sold at
auction. Vehicle Control also manages five fuel sites located throughout the Town,
ensuring compliance with the Suffolk County Sanitary Code and NYS DEC regulations.
The fuel sites are used in the operation of Town vehicles and equipment as well as
some local first responder vehicles. Additionally, all oversight of underground and above
ground tanks owned by the Town of Brookhaven fall under the purview of this Division,
to ensure compliance with SCDHS regulations as well as the NYSDEC.
lmpounds’ Abandoned Vehicles Division - The Abandoned Vehicles Division isresponsible
for handling complaints received by residents and local law enforcement agencies,
resulting in the removal and disposition of abandoned vehicles throughout the Town of
Brookhaven, in accordance with New York State Vehicle and Traffic Law. Storing
53

64.text:
vehicles impounded reported by the Suffolk County Police Department or the Suffolk
County Sheriffs Office as road hazards or 511's and auctioning or recycling said
vehicles when not redeemed by their owner. Impounded vehicles are also provided to
fire districts for use in their various drills.
Central Reproduction and the Mailing Divwision- Central Reproduction provides daily
print copies of various documents, brochures, pamphlets and flyers requested by all
departments throughout the Town, including the Annual Operating and Capital Budget
Books. Mailroom staff are responsible for the distribution of both internal and extemal
mail and deliveries to all Town facilities throughout Brookhaven.
Office of the Town Histonan — Serves as primary repository for Brookhaven's historical
records excluding those records maintained by the Town Clerk. Historian provides
research services to other Town Departments and private researchers who wish to use
the Town's collections. Educational programs to outside organizations and schools can
be pre-arranged. The Histonan serves as a member of the Historic District Advisory
Committee and submits reports anrwally to the New York State Historian. The Town
Historian also serves as the liaison to the Town's Black History Commission, which
hosts a Black History Awards Celebration in February as well as an Annual Juneteenth
Celebration for all Town of Brookhaven residents.
Youth B         Divisi
The Youth Bureau's INTERFACE program works with businesses and non-profit
agencies to provide a vanety of programs to Brookhaven Town Youth, including the free
Prom Dress program, the Holiday Toy Drives, Back to School Supply Drive, Winter Coat
Drive and Thanksgiving Food Drive. The Youth Bureau also runs the Safe Summer
Nights Program at 3 Town Parks, serving young individuals throughout Brookhaven. In
addition, the Youth Bureau has a Vocational program to support teens and young adults
in identifying updated job postings and employment skills on a weekly basis.
Senior Citizens Division and Nutrition Program. provides support, workshops and
recreational opportunities to Brookhaven’'s 65,000 seniors, with services designed to
promote and enrich the quality of life for senior citizens. Programs include the Home
Maintenance’ Repair Program, Helpline Telephone Reassurance Program for the
Homebound, the Senior Nutrition Program, a host of senior citizens clubs, and the
Annual two-day Senior Picnic, attended by approximately 1,200 seniors each day. The
Town's Senior Center offers daily workshops, activities, exercise programs, games, DJ
dances, and a variety of other programs for the Town's Senior population.
Women's Senices Division- provides an array of supportive services for women in crisis
or transition including the Dress for Success program, designed to assist women by
providing relevant training, professional clothing and valuable resources to gain and
retain employment. The Division of Women's Services partners with over 250 referral
agencies throughout Brookhaven Town and Long Island. The Annual Women's
Conference and Women's Recognition Awards Night are well attended events
showcasing the varied achievements and services available to women throughout the
Brookhaven community.

65.text:
Veterans Services Divisian- provides outreach and support for Brookhaven veterans and
their families in collaboraton with Suffolk County through a Veterans Services Officer
assigned to the Town of Brookhaven. Veterans receive assistance in determining which
benefits they are entitled to and provided help with completing applications and
obtaining referrals. The Town of Brookhaven provides a stipend to each chartered VFW
Post located within the Town at our Annual Veterans Appreciation Luncheon in
November. In 2024 the Town and County sponsored a Veterans Resource Fair which,
due to its huge success, has become an annual event.

Department Accomplishments for 2026

The Deparment of General Services contracted with an Engineering Firm and
established the first-ever Tank Compliance Program, aimed at better managing the
300+UST's & AST's, maintaining up-to-date permits, and ensuring compliance
with State and County regulations. Building on this initiative, our goal of receiving a
comprehensive report was successful. The department is also responsible for
coordination, oversight and execution of a host of annual events such as the Health
& Vellness Fair, Women's Conference, Martn Luther King Luncheon, Veterans
Resource Fair, Senior Picnic, Youth Awards, Women's Recognition Night, Holiday Toy
Drive, Coat Drive, Food Drives, Juneteenth BBQ, 6” Precinct-Level Advisory Board
Community meeting and many other workshops and events.

years or older, which will improve reliability, reduce repair and maintenance

resulting in a reduced environmental impact and carbon footprint.

mileage vehicles from service and replacing them with new and more efficient

DEPARTMENT OF HIGHWAY
Mission Statement:
To maintain, repair and reconstruct Town-owned roads, drainage systems, culverts,
bridges, sluiceways and boardwalks. Under New York State Highway Law, it is the
responsibility of the Superintendent to cause the above to be kept in good repair
and free from obstructions caused by snow; to inspect the highways; to employ such
persons as may be necessary for the maintenance and repair of Town highways; to
provide for the supervision of such persons; to construct and keep in repair sluices
and culverts; to cause the waterways, bridges and culverts to be kept open; to cause
loose stones lying in the beaten track of every Town highway to be removed; to
cause briars, brush and noxious weeds growing within the bounds of Town highways
to be cut and removed; to attend public meetings called by the Department of
Transportation; to maintain all sidewalks in the Town; and to perform such duties
and have such powers as may be imposed or conferred by law, or the rules and
regulations of the Department of Transportation.
Department Description
Highway: The Highway Department is responsible for over 3,617 lane miles of
roadway throughout the Town of Brookhaven, making it the third largest roadway
system in New York State. The Department is responsible for the day-to-day
maintenance of the roadways, and undertakes removal of dead, damaged and
dangerous trees in Town right-of-way areas. The Highway Department receives over
1,000 warranted requests for tree removal on an annual basis. Other areas of
responsibility for the Highway Department include the identification and associated
mitigation of drainage problems as well as repairing concrete curbs, handicap
ramps, sidewalks and driveway aprons.
Traffic Safety. The Division of Traffic Safety's mission is to maintain and improve
traffic safety on Brookhaven roadways by reducing traffic related accidents and
injuries through traffic engineering and traffic safety education. The major
functions of the Division include maintenance and installation of traffic control
devices such as traffic signals, pavement markings, signage and guiderail. These
devices are implemented for accident prevention, traffic complaint problem solving
and resolution. Traffic Safety education programs include a child passenger safety
program to inspect and ensure proper installation of child safety seats as well as an
elementary school-age educational program held at our Safety Town facility in
Holtsville. This program teaches students pedestrian, bicycle and vehicle safety. We
also provide a teen driver safety program that teaches teens the dangers of impaired
and distracted driving, and an adult defensive driving education program which may
reduce the cost of car insurance or points on a license.
88

99.text:
Streetlighting- The Division of Streetlighting maintains the streetlights on all Town
roadways, as well as all County and State Highways (except Sunrise Highway, the
Long Island Expressway and those within Incorporated Villages), At the present time,
there are approximately 50,000 streetlights in the Town of Brookhaven. Each of
these lights have been mapped by the Global Positioning System (GPS) and entered
inte our priority Streetlighting Inventory and Maintenance System (SIMS). SIMS is
used to track the status of each light, its maintenance history, wattage, etc., as
well as tracking warehouse inventory. The Streetlighting Division is nearing the
completion of replacing all 48,000 inefficient and outdated low and high-pressure
sodium streetlights and poles that currently exist across the Town with new, energy-
efficient and cost-effective Light Emitting Diodes (LED) streetlights. The mew LED
lights aré up to 60 percent more efficient, have an estimated lifespan of up to 20
years and require much less maintenance, which equates to recurring annual savings
in electricity. The Division also installed Ubicell Smart Photocells on major roads.
These smart photocells inform the Division if a light does not work so the light can
be repaired in a timely manner. Streetlighting continues to replace outdated or
damaged underground wiring for the Post Top streetlights in the Town of
Brookhaven.
Stormwater Management- The Division of Stormwater Management acts as the
operator of the Town's MS4 (Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System). This Division
designs a suite of programs and practices that minimize and prevents pollution of
surface waters from stormwater. Regular upgrades to our drainage infrastructure
are designed to reduce pollution and mitigate flood hazards. All stormwater
infrastructure, including outfalls to surface water and catch basins, is mapped in
the Town's GIS. The Division is also responsible for the design and implementation
of large-scale stormwater mitigation projects, which improves water quality and
enhances natural environs.

DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
Mission Statement:

The mission of the Department of Housing and Community Development is to provide
services to Town residents through a variety of programs using federal, state, and local
grant funding. The Department continues to help those families in need of housing
assistance and provides programs to diverse populations within the Town of
Brookhaven.

Department Description

The Department of Housing and Community Development administers the Federal
Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program, HOME Investment Partnership
Grant, Emergency Solution Grant (E5G), Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS
Program (HOPWA), HOME-ARP American Rescue Program, Housing Choice Voucher
Program (HCV), Foster Youth to Independence Program (Fil), and Family Self
Sufficiency Program (F535).

« The CDBG Program is used to fund various projects including removal of
architectural barriers to accessibility, housing rehabilitation, parks and public
works improvements, and several youth and family counseling service
organizations.

« The Residential Rehabilitation Program provides a zero percent interest deferred
loan to any income eligible homeowner in need of a handicap ramp or handicap
lift to enhance access to their home. Additionally, the Rehabilitation Program
provides repairs to owner-occupied single-family homes in the Town, thereby
stabilizing or increasing home values. Repairs can be made on any part of the
home from the chimney to the sanitary system. This program addresses any code
issues first.

« The HOME Program funds a wide range of activities including building and
rehabilitating affordable housing for homeownership opportunities. In addition,
the funds assist low-income first-time homebuyers with down payment
assistance.

* ESG funding is used to assist individuals/families who are homeless or on the
verge of becoming homeless.

« The HOPWA program provides housing assistance and related supportive services
to meet the housing needs of low-income individuals and their families living
with HIV/AIDS.

® The HOME-ARP American Rescue Program assists individuals/families who are
homeless or on the verge of becoming homeless and other qualifying populations

100

141.text:
with rental assistance.

® The Housing Choice Voucher Program operates on an annual budget of
approximately $20,000,000 and currently has the capacity to subsidize over 994
rental units monthly. Through the Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program, the
department also administers Emergency Housing Vouchers (EHV) and Foster
Youth to Independence (FY l)¥ouchers.

« The Family Self-Sufficiency (FS5) Program is a five-year voluntary program
offered to Housing Choice Voucher individuals and families to assist them on the
path to self-sufficiency and economic independence.

« The department provides assistance to people with disabilities by providing
referrals and advocating to ensure smooth transition to the service(s) they may
require,

« Suffolk County 72H Program provides affordable housing opportunities through
the transfer of properties from the County to the Town for affordable housing
purposes. The Town works with several not-for-profit organizations to Build and
sell homes to income eligible families in the Town of Brookhaven.

Department Accomplishments for 2026
® Several community projects were completed through the Federal Community
Development Programs, such as:

> ADA Improvements throughout the town and villages.

> Removal of architectural barriers throughout the Town.

© Installed ADA curb ramps on Hillside Avenue in the Village of Patchosue
and Rocketship Park in the Village of Port Jefferson.

> Park improvements were completed at St. Michael's Recreation Center

DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
Mission Statement:

The Town of Brookhaven Department of Information Technology (IT) is committed to
using technology to improve lives. We strive to deliver secure, efficient services, foster
innovation, and maintain transparency for the benefit of our community.
Department Description
The IT Department at the Town of Brookhaven manages and maintains computer and
telephony systems, offers technical support to employees, ensures data security, and
implements technology solutions to enhance efficiency and communication within the
Town and with the community we serve.
Department Accomplishments for 2026
During 2026, the Department of Information Technology managed more than 70
formally tracked technology initiatives while continuing to provide daily technical
support and maintain the Town's critical systems, infrastructure, and digital services.

« Completed the Town-wide implementation of the Infor Land Management
System, modernizing permitting and land-use workflows and expanding online
services for residents, businesses, and multiple Town departments.

« Established a new ArcGlS Enterprise environment and modernized the Town's
geographic information systems, including cloud infrastructure, applications,
data processes, legacy-script conversion, and access to updated aerial imagery
and analysis tools.

« Strengthened the Town's cybersecurity posture by implementing managed
detection and response services, completing the New York State DHSES Cyber
Incident Response Team Rapid Risk Assessment, and advancing network
segmentation, endpoint protection, identity management, and mobile-device
security.

« Eliminated more than 160 legacy copper telephone lines, reducing unnecessary
infrastructure and producing approximately $50,000 in annual recurring savings,
while continuing to optimize telecommunications, software licensing, and
technology accounts.

* Modemized IT service delivery through improvements to the ServiceNow
employee portal, centralized assignment and tracking of IT work, standardized
customer communications, enhanced reporting, and expanded knowledge
resources.

« Launched a coordinated series of initiatives to modernize wireless connectivity
and network infrastructure at Town Hall, beaches, parks, recreational locations,
offices, and remote facilities. This included establishing individual projects and

135

147.text:
beginning the assessment, planning, design, and procurement work necessary to
support implementation during 2027 and beyond.

* Supported technology modernization across the Town Clerk, Finance, Assessor,
Parks, Public Safety, Highway, Animal Shelter, Fire Prevention, Waste
Management, and other operating departments through improved business
systems, mobile connectivity, digital workflows, data services, and specialized
applications.

* Improved technology governance and operational efficiency through formal
project portfolio tracking, infrastructure and equipment inventories, software
and license reviews, and more structured technology procurement and vendor
management.

Department Goals for 2027

* Migrate the Town's legacy telephone system to a modern cloud-based platform
to improve reliability, resiliency, administration, and supportability.

® Migrate the Town's electronic document management system from its current
hosted environment to a modern cloud-based platform, improving accessibility,
supportability, and long-term system management.

« Implement network access controls to improve visibility into devices connected
to the Town network, enforce security policies, and strengthen network
segmentation.

» Deploy an enterprise-wide password management solution to improve the
security, oversight, and controlled sharing of administrative, departmental, and
other sensitive credentials.

» Review the Town's mobile-device footprint, service assignments, and recurring
licensing costs, and develop an internal portal to centralize device inventory,
requests, approvals, assignments, and lifecycle management.

» Advance wireless connectivity and network infrastructure improvements at Town
Hall, beaches, parks, recreational locations, offices, and remote facilities.

» Consolidate fleet management operations from two separate systems into the
Town's existing enterprise work order management platform, creating a
consistent process for vehicle maintenance, asset tracking, and reporting.

« Implement new digital workflows and online service capabilities for the Town
Clerk's Office to improve public access and streamline internal processing.

« Transition the Town to a modern code publishing and hosting platform to improve
public access to the Town Code and streamline the publication and maintenance
of legislative updates.

« Continue improving IT service delivery by expanding self-service resources,
strengthening request intake and tracking, improving reporting, and bringing
more departmental technology work into consistent and measurable workflows.

DEPARTMENT OF LAW
Mission Statement:
To provide legal counsel to all government entities within the Town of Brookhaven. The
Department also efficiently and effectively enforces the Town Code to aid in protecting
the health, safety, and welfare of the residents of the Town of Brookhaven.
Department Description
The Department of Law acts as general in-house legal counsel to all government entities
within the Town of Brookhaven, providing legal advice, defending lawsuits, and
prosecuting violations of the Town Code. The Department handles the following
categories of work:
Investigations: investigates and prosecutes violations of the Town Code,
Contracts & Leases- negotiates, drafts, and enforces all contractual relationships with
the Town. Also collects judgments and handles contract litigation.
Insurance and Risk Management- processes, adjusts, and defends all non-land use
claims against the Town of Brookhaven. Prepares legal papers, conducts depositions,
and attends court appearances to protect the interests of the Town.
Special Districts- handles the legal mechanism used to deliver specific services to
residents that are not being provided on a Town-wide basis, The Town has been
consolidating districts to be more efficient and cost effective.
Parking Violations Bureau- responsible for processing and resolution of parking citations
issued by all law enforcement agencies within the Town, issuing employee ID badges
and actively participating in the adjudication process at monthly hearings.
Land Management- assists the Town in acquiring open space and conducting the
transactions involved in the process. Responsibilities include managing properties that
have been acquired, donated, or dedicated for open space purposes as well as properties
dedicated to the Town’s Nature Preserve System. This includes inspecting Town
properties and identifying clearing and encroachment violations.
Planning and Zoning represents the Board of Zoning Appeals at hearings and in
litigation matters. Work with Planning Department staff on land use applications and
plans. Advise the Building Division on all matters.

DEPARTMENT OF PARKS, RECREATION &
SPORTS,  & CULTURAL RESOURCES
Mission Statement:

The Department of Parks and Recreation provides year-round amenities, services and
varied athletic and recreation programs to all residents of the Town of Brookhaven. The
Parks Department strives to provide the very best that Brookhaven and Long Island has to

offer and to enhance the quality of life for our residents.
Department Description
The Town of Brookhaven Parks Department is a year-round operation that maintains over 150
facilities throughout the Town including, but not limited to:

e Parks

« Ballfields

« Grass Cutting

« Town Hall Building & Facilities

« Beaches

* Pools

« Marinas

« Recreation Centers

« Community Events and Charity Events

« Construction/Capital Projects

« Historic Structures

* Snow Plowing

Recreation programs include:

« Baseball League - Summer/Fall & Tournaments - 5,000 players

« Soccer League - Summer - 2,000 players

« Basketball - Summer - 1,500 players

« Adult Softball - Spring through Fall - 2,500 players

« Swimming Lessons - 2,000 participants

« Girls Softball Fastpitch Program - 1,000 players

* Summer Camps and Special Recreation Programs - Approximately 1,500 participants

* Recreation Center Programs - Year-Round - 6,000 participants

« Pickleball Programs - Leagues, Clinics, and Lessons - 300 participants

The Town of Brookhaven Parks Department also provides the service of selling approximately
58,000 Virtual Annual Parking Permits which allows residents to park at Town of
Brookhaven Beaches, Parks, or Pools without having to pay a daily Parking Meter fee.

204.text:
DEPARTMENT OF PLANNING, BUILDING, &
ENVIRONMENTAL
Mission Statement:
To provide optimal and effective land use within the Town of Brookhaven. To protect
and enhance the quality of life in Brookhaven Town through engaging in community-
based planning, environmental stewardship and working to enhance citizen education
and participation.
Department Description
The Department is divided into several divisions:
Planning Division- The Planning Division works to provide for the orderly growth and
development of the Town of Brookhaven through reviewing proposals for subdivision,
land division, site plans, road improvements and changes of use to ensure that projects
incorporate best planning practices. The Planning Division also conducts land use
studies which update the Town's Comprehensive Plan and provides planning and land
use recommendations to both the Planning and Town Boards.
Building Division- The Building Division reviews building permit applications and plans
for the issuance of permits for new construction and alteration to existing buildings and
structures. It is the only jurisdiction tasked with assuring that all Federal, State, County
and Town jurisdictional requirements are met regarding the improvements to parcels
with the Town. The Division inspects for compliance with the NYS Uniform Code and
Town Codes and issues Certificates of Occupancy. The Division also responds to
violations and takes actions necessary to compel violators into compliance.
Division of Engineering - The Engineering Division works directly with the Planning
Division and the Division of Environmental Protection. They perform all inspections as
they pertain to site work on all site plans, subdivisions and single-family home
construction. In addition, the Division is responsible for reviewing all grading and
drainage plans for subdivisions and site plans. Engineering is also responsible for all
SWPPP conditional releases as well as working with an engineer and applicants for all
SWPPP applications.
Division _of Environmental Protection- The Division of Environmental Protection is
charged with the administration, management, and implementation of all matters
pertaining to the protection and preservation of the environment. This includes the
issuance of Wetlands/Coastal Erosion Hazard Area (CEHA) Permits and Mastic Beach
Stick Dock Permits. The Division is responsible for addressing activities that may impair,
damage, or destroy natural resources; promoting environmental stewardship through
154

205.text:
education and outreach; and administering programs that support the restoration of
shellfish populations and the advancement of aquaculture initiatives.

Planning Board- |n 2024, the Town Board assumed the roles and responsibilities of the
Planning Board. As such, the Town Board as the Planning Board hears all applications
that pertain to Planning. In addition, applicants can now file both Change of Zones and
Site Plans simultaneously which in turn will provide a more expeditious review and
approval process.

Historic District Review Committee- The Historic District Review Committee advises
the various boards on all matters relating to existing historic districts or historic
landmarks.

Special Districts: Erosion Control and Dock- The Erosion Control and Dock Districts
provide services specifically to the residents of these districts, who reimburse the Town
for those services through tax levies.

Department Accomplishments for 2026

« Successfully worked with the Department of Information Technology on the
implementation and roll out of the Infor Land Management System.

* Reviewed and presented/approved approximately 200 planning applications.
This includes both projects presented to the Planning Board, Town Board and
administrative approvals.

« Continue to cut down review times by merging the application process allowing
COZ and Site plans to be submitted and reviewed together, saving applicants
up to a year in review,

« Made significant progress on improvements and upgrades to the Sewer District
2 and have identified additional improvements and upgrades to make.

« Obtained all permits and approvals for the Leaching pool expansion project.

« Began work on the North Shore Local Waterfront Revitalization Program.

* Created the Mastic Beach Sewer District and awarded bid for construction of
the Sewer Treatment Plant.

« Implemented energy efficiency initiatives throughout the Town.

« Worked with Suffolk County, USACE and NYSDEC to have the FIMI project
merged into the FIMP program to ensure routine renourishment will take place.

* Purchased and raised approximately 1.5 million hard clams and nearly 1.5
million oysters for the Shellfish Management Program.

« Planted nearly 1.6 Million Hard Clams and Oysters seed throughout the Town's
waterways including Bellport Bay, Moriches Bay, Mt. Sinai Harbor, along the
Carmens River and Stonybrook Yacht Club, Some were planted by our DEP staff
while others were given to Not for Profit groups to plant in local waterways.

« Returned 140 bags of oyster cages back to the water for future growth.

206.text:
* Early data indicated tnat oysters were removing about 50% of the
microalgae, greatly improving water quality.

« Completed the Mastic Beach Saltmarsh Restoration plans and permits and
submitted final project report to the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation.

« Continue to work with USACE to extend the project area of their Coastal
Process Feature in Mastic Beach to include the full 147 area of saltmarsh
habitat, including all restoration costs, boardwalk installation and property
acquisitions.

« Secured numerous environmental grants that will bring environmental benefits,
including habitat restoration, invasive species removal, and promoting
diadromous fish migration.

« Continued working with a Master Developer for the revitalization of
Neighborhood Road area in Mastic Beach.

« Implemented code updates and changes to Chapters 25 & 81 to help streamline
department processes.

* Continue working with Mastic Beach homeowner's and the USACE for the house
raising initiatives through FIMP.

® Worked with the USACE to begin implementing the FIMP pilot program to
elevate 150 houses in Mastic Beach.

® Continued the Licensing Agreement with the Setauket Harbor Task Force, a
not-for-profit, for growing Spat on Shell (SOS) at the Shore Road Marina.

« Continuing the Licensing Agreement with the Mastic Beach Conservancy to grow
50S in Marina 5.

» Developed two additional Aquaculture Farms in the Narrows for Narrow Bay
Aquaculture and Doall Aquaculture.

« Continuation of the oyster reef in the FOBB Management Area.

« The department took over all the SWPPP applications to help make the process
with the site plan review more streamlined and efficient.

Building Division Accomplishments 2026

« Processed over 13,00 permits and issued over 1,500 certificates of occupancy.

« Implemented same day permit issuance for pools and decks.

« Coordinated with the Call Center to create FAQ spreadsheet to improve
responses to residents’ inquiries.

« Redirected call center calls to reduce hold times, including creating an IT-
supported hunt group with office assistance to ensure quicker responses to
public questions.

» Created a group of office assistants to respond to online inquiries at the
building info web-email.

» Established designated commercial inspector areas.

156

207.text:
* Demolition evaluations and Unsafe Structure complaints are completed and
inspected by each Building Inspector in a specific sector, eliminating the
backlog of submitting the written reports.

* Streamlined Accessory Apartment License applications and renewals to fast-
track the process by eliminating the need for appearance before the Accessory
Apartment Review Board, Applicants now submit license applications together
with building permit applications concurrently, reducing the wait time for
review.

« Worked with the Chief Building Inspector to enhance Division efficiency and
further streamline application and permit processes for improved public
accessibility.

» Opened the building division up for full public access helping to streamline
processes and assist residents.

Department Goals for 2027

* Continue to pursue grants to help fund environmental programs.

« Continue to work on the Local Waterfront Revitalization Plan for the North
Shore of Brookhaven.

« Continue the development of the Mastic Beach Sewer District.

e Begin construction for the Leaching Pool Expansion at Sewer District 2.

« Complete the Swan Lake Management Plan.

« Continue working on the Wildlife Tunnels at Cedar Beach

* Remove invasive species from Cedar Beach, West Meadow Beach and around
Swan River.

® Continue working with Columbia University on their coastal flooding plan
project.

* Continue the work on the Carmans River Trail Design. Trail to be completed in
2028.

« Werking to get permitted plans for the Swan River Preserve restoration.

e Perform a 10-day Shellfish survey throughout the Patchogue and Bellport Bays,
for principally, hard clams, as well as razor clams and stout razor clams.

« Continue to encourage reduced reliance on fossil fuels for new buildings.

« Work with developers, engineers, attorneys and contractors to promote
development while protecting the safety, health and welfare of the public.

«® Encourage additional “Green” features in development plans.

« Continue to grow and plant clams and oysters throughout the North and South
Shores to improve the water quality.

« (Create new and innovative ways to educate residents and raise awareness on
environmental issues.

« Complete the Terrel River fish passage plans.

208.text:
® Hopefully expand the Towns shellfish facility to include a Hatchery so we can
raise and grow our own seed, eliminating the need to purchase from outside
SOUTCEsS.

« Continue to implement energy efficiency initiatives throughout the Town.

« Continue to update the Codes in Chapter &5 and Chapter 871.

e Continue to work on the Brookhaven Town Comprehensive Plan to support the
revitalization of all Downtown areas throughout the Town of Brookhaven.

« Continue to upgrade Sewer District Number 2 building.

« Implement the Port Jefferson Station Downtown Revitalization Plan along with
the County to bring sewers down to the business district of Route 172.

e Continue with the Master Developer towards revitalization of Neighborhood
Road in Mastic Beach (NRRA).

® Complete the North Shore LWRP which would merge with the South Shore LWRP
giving the town a full Local Water Revitalization plan.

® Modermization and simplification of department applications will lead to
increased conversion rates, productivity enhancement, and an improved user
experience.

« Continue to work with NYS to select eligible projects to be funded through the
NY Forward Grant in the North Bellport Community.

e Continue to work with the USACE to implement the FIMP Pilot Program in
Mastic Beach.

« Begin the Sheepen Peninsula saltmarsh restoration,

Building Division Goals 2027

» Fully implement, refine, and optimize the new INFOR Land Management System
to create a more efficient and user-friendly application, permitting, and review
process.

s Provide comprehensive training for Town staff and external stakeholders,
including expeditors, builders, contractors, commercial and residential
applicants, and the general public.

« Streamline the application and review process by reducing unnecessary steps,
improving workflow, and shortening overall processing and review timeframes.

« Consolidate departmental reviews into one unified system, improving
communication and coordination among Town departments and eliminating
duplicative processes.

* Improve the applicant experience by providing a more transparent, accessible,
and user-friendly process from initial application through final approval.

« Implement a simplified and standardized fee schedule that establishes clear
and consistent fee parameters and makes it easier for applicants to determine
the anticipated cost of proposed property improvements.

209.text:
« Increase transparency and predictability of costs so residents, businesses,
contractors, and other applicants can better understand applicable fees at the
beginning of the process.

* Increase Town revenues through improved fee assessment and collection,
ensuring that applicable fees are accurately and consistently calculated,
tracked, and collected.

» Establish a more reliable revenue stream through the combination of the new
fee structure and INFOR’s improved tracking and accountability.

» Create greater efficiencies Town-wide by integrating systems, improving
accountability, reducing processing times, and providing faster and more
consistent service to the public.

* All Code Enforcement Officer (CEO) training will continue, to ensure
compliance with the new New York State Code revisions.

« Review and update Chapter 85 to make Building Division procedures more
efficient.

226.text:
DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY
Mission Statement:
To ensure the protection, safety and security needs of our residents and the Town's
employees. Members of the Department are committed to providing the residents of
Brookhaven with the most prompt, courteous and efficient response to their concerns
and complaints.
Department Description
The Department of Public Safety is comprised of the Division of Code Enforcement,
Division of Harbors and Waterways, Division of Fire Prevention, the Office of
Occupational Health and Safety, the Animal Shelter, and General Aviation. The
Department meets the challenges of operating a safe and economically viable airport
and to raise the level of awareness and support for the Town’s Animal Shelter and
Adoption Center. Department of Public Safety's additional responsibilities include the
Tow Truck and Taxi Licensing Section and Noise Variances.
Division of Code Enforcement- The Division of Code Enforcement is responsible for all
uniformed enforcement and security activity within the Town. The Division includes the
Town Public Safety Agents, whose main responsibilities include the security of all Town
properties and facilities such as buildings, parks, and marinas as well as the
enforcement of appropriate Town Code violations. Public Safety Agents also assist local
law enforcement with the impounding of vehicles deemed as road hazards and in
violation of Section 511 of the Vehicle & Traffic Law.
Division of Harbors and Woterways- The Division of Harbors and Waterways oversees
waterway operations for more than 153 miles of coastline, encompassing a water
surface area of 272 square miles on both the North and South Shores. The
Harbormasters, as sworn Peace Officers, enforce the New York State Navigation Law,
the Environmental Conservation Law, as well as applicable Brookhaven Town
Ordinances. Other responsibilities include the installation and maintenance of several
hundred navigational aids in our waterways, responding to all emergency calls,
including all maydays, missing/injured persons and sinking/disabled vessels occurring
on our waterways and extensive shellfish enforcement. The Division supervises and
administers the Town's pump-out services to our boating population and acts as liaison
for the Port Jefferson Harbor Commission for communication and administrative
purposes.
Division of Fire Prevention- The Division of Fire Prevention is a multifaceted unit within
the Department of Public Safety. Fire Marshals are sworn Peace Officers and Certified
Code Enforcement Officials. Fire prevention, life safety and enforcement of state and
local codes are a few of the core responsibilities of the Division, which are achieved in
a variety of ways. Review of plan submissions, issuance of permits/ permissions related
26

227.text:
to new construction, alterations and fire protection systems, inspection of premises
once installations are complete, as well as annual and triennial inspection of public and
privately-owned commercial buildings are all methods utilized to ensure compliance
and, thus, general life safety. As the Hazardous Materials Response Team for the 38
volunteer fire departments within the Town, the Division of Fire Prevention Fire
Marshals are New York State certified Hazardous Materials Technicians. The team
responds to and mitigates hazardous materials incidents. As New York State certified
fire investigators, Fire Marshals respond to all fires within the Town to determine the
origin and cause of every fire that occurs within the Town. The Division provides fire
prevention and life safety education by giving presentations to school age groups,
adult/senior citizen organizations, homeowners associations, and at fire department
open house events. The Office of Emergency Management (OEM) is a section within the
Division of Fire Prevention and is charged with coordinating services with State, County,
tribal communities, local municipalities, school districts and various Town of
Brookhaven Departments and agencies to assure uninhibited operations in the event of
any man-made or natural disasters. The OEM ensures the rules and regulations of FEMA
and NYS Department of Homeland Security are followed, and utilizes the protocols
established by the National Incident Management System (MIMS),
Occupational Safety & Health (Senior Safety Officer)- Occupational Safety and Health
is tasked with ensuring a safe and hazard- free work environment and to ensure the
safety and health of the active workforce by providing mandated training to employees,
administering the Town's health and safety programs, and serve as liaison to the Public
Employee Safety and Health (PESH) Bureau. The Senior Safety Officer also maintains
the AED program and conducts various seminars and meetings with employees to
enhance workplace safety and compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
Taxi & Tow Truck Licensing Administrators- Staff assigned to Public Safety
administration are responsible for the maintenance and regulation of the towing and
taxi industries within the Town by providing and securing documentation for the same.
The staff also oversees and coordinates all steps in the licensing process between the
Town's Building Division, Law Department, Fire Marshal, and Vehicle Control Division.
Additionally, any code violations involving tow trucks and taxicabs are reported to the
appropriate department for follow up investigation and enforcement purposes.
Chapters 66 and 67 of the Town Code detail tow truck and taxicab codification.
Division of Animal Shelter - The Division of Animal Shelter and Adoption Center
facilitates the placement of stray and surrendered animals into desirable homes through
the cooperative efforts of public entities dedicated to the welfare of animals. The
shelter promotes the prevention of overpopulation through spay and neuter programs.
lt conducts humane education and community programs. The shelter also handles
constituent reports of stray dogs, aggressive animals, sick/injured cats and animal
hoarding locations.
Division of General Aviation - The Division of General Aviation is located at Brookhaven
Calabro Airport in Shirley. The buildings, runways and taxiways are maintained to
ensure the safety of aviation-related users, residents, and visitors. Additional
217

228.text:
responsibilities include oversight of the various private aviation-related businesses on
airport property, flight operations of air traffic utilization, and establishing a liaison
with the Federal Aviation Administration.

Department Accomplishments for 2026

Code Enforcement Division

« Continued to answer numerous quality of life complaints for the constituents of
Brookhaven.

e Reduced the number of complaints at our North Shore Beach and road endings.

* Expanded the Beach Guard positions to address issues at our North Shore Beaches
and  road  endings, eliminating costs associated with private security, while
increasing revenue.

« Assisted the communities with numerous public events with duties such as traffic
control, patrols, and parking enforcement.

» Town Public Safety Agents performed life saving measures at the Town of
Brookhaven Senior Picnic.

Harbors & Waterways Division

« Awarded coveted Port Security Grant and received delivery of a new south
shore 31" patrol boat which was put into service in the spring of 2026.

257.text:
OFFICE OF THE RECEIVER OF TAXES
Mission Statement:
The Receiver of Taxes is an elected official whose responsibilities include the printing
and delivery of tax statements and the collection and distribution of tax funds. The
Receiver of Taxes keeps the public informed and is available to answer inquiries.
Department Description
The Office of the Tax Receiver collects property taxes for school districts, Suffolk
County, Brookhaven Town, fire districts, refuse districts, and library districts. — In
processing payments, the department accepts cash and checks, electronic funds, and
credit cards. The office receives payments, balances transactions, makes deposits,
records payments, adjusts and corrects tax bills, issues refunds, and interacts with
banking institutions and other governmental entities. The Tax Receiver’s office mails
bills, receipts, reminders, delinquent notices, and handles protested checks and
records apportionments on the tax roll.
Department Accomplishments for 2026
« Reorganized office staff to maintain staffing levels at reduced cost.
« Further enhanced online payment opportunities and payment processing.
« Worked with municipalities and Villages within Brookhaven Town and Suffolk
County to provide tax collection services and enhancements.
« Increased online payment activity by more than 15 percent.
« Continued to collect a duplicate bill fee for commercial entities who request an
additional copy of a tax bill.
« Mailed pie charts with the tax bills or receipts to illustrate the allocation of tax
dollars.
* Reduced costs associated with the preparation and mailing of required tax
receipts.
» Adjusted banking to reduce costs for deposit collection.
« Increased available online payment history for taxpayer information purposes.
« Increased online tax history available for residential and commercial customers.
Department Goals for 2027
« Continue community outreach information and resources.

OFFICE OF THE TOWN CLERK

Mission Statement:
To serve the present and future needs of the residents of the Town of Brookhaven, the
Town Supervisor, the Town Council, and all other entities of Town Government.
Department Description
The Office of the Town Clerk is responsible for recording all activities of Town
government and maintaining all associated documents.
In addition, the Town Clerk:

« is the Recording Secretary of the Town Board

» is the Records Management Officer and Archivist of the Town

» is the Registrar of Vital Statistics

» acts a5 depository for agency and special district filings

» initiated and oversees the Central Scanning Repository

« dockets and files all legal actions and legal matters involving the Town and its

agencies

* performs genealogical searches upon request

* oversees bingo inspectors and reports required by New York State

« issues licenses and permits for handicapped parking, outdoor assemblage,

parades, amusements/events, beach buggy, shellfish, wooden walks, peddlers,
pigeons, dogs and pooch passes

« assigns boat slips for the five Town Marinas and maintains the accompanying

waiting lists
Department Accomplishments for 2026
« Partnered with the IT Department to develop an improved Dog Licensing system
to increase efficiencies in staff processing and ease of use for residents.

* Renewed the Town's agreement with NYSDEC to issue hunting and fishing permits
to Brookhaven Town residents at Town Hall.

« Initiated a new workflow system for Municipal Notices of Cannabis License
Applications Notifications, that allow for departments to analyze and submit
determinations on applications within the state deadline requirements.

s Increased Shared Services throughout the town by entering into agreements with
other municipalities and community group to store physical records at the
Town's Regional Record Center

« Expanded on the Town Clerk's initiate to share the Town's History with monthly
episodes of “Talking History with the Town Clerk.”

« Continued with the Town Clerk’s commitment to Community Outreach by holding
monthly Library Mobile Office Hours, attending Civic Association Meetings, and

253

264.text:
hosting community events, including a National Night Out event with over 2,500
attendees and the 12" Annual Run the Farm with 227 runners and over $15,000
raised,

Department Goals for 2027

« Enter into intermunicipal agreements with the villages, libraries, fire districts
and other special districts for storage of physical records at the Regional Record
Center.

« Work with the Town’s Historian to inventory any records, artifacts, etc. received
from Historic Societies to preserve in the renovated historic records vault.

« Security upgrades to the Town Clerk's office, including renovations of the public-
facing counter, access control, and modifications of the waiting area to promote
privacy during transactions.

» Increase Town Clerk Services offered online by integrating our applications and
processing into a shared town software application.

» Sean and archive Highway Administration, Finance, and Planning Department
records.

» Implement new department-wide software program to replace aging legacy
program.

DEPARTMENT OF RECYCLING AND SUSTAINABLE
MATERIALS MANAGEMENT
Mission Statement:
To provide our residents with comprehensive and innovative programs that, in addition
to being economically sound and environmentally safe, help to create a change in how
society thinks about the use of natural resources and environmental protection. The
Department seeks a systemic approach to using and reusing materials more productively
over their life cycle.
Department Description
The Department oversees one of the largest municipal waste management programs in
the State of New York. It is responsible for the management of residential solid waste
collection and the management of facilities including oversight of: a Materials Recycling
Facility (MRF), a STOP program (Stop Throwing Out Pollutants) for hazardous household
wastes, a transfer station, a landfill constructed te current standards that provides a
disposal option for residential waste to energy ash and other recycling residues, a yard
waste processing area and a residential drop-off site. The Department also oversees
management of the Manorville Composting Facility, Town Sanitation Code enforcement,
roadside and littered property cleanups, abandoned building demolitions, and collection
of special materials from residences such as certain bulk items and scrap metal items.
The Department promotes material reduction, reuse, recycling and proper disposal of
waste. The Department also has active public information, outreach and participation
initiatives for residents, businesses, schools, and institutions throughout the Town.
Department Accomplishments for 2026
Reuse
» Continued agreements with various non-profit organizations to reduce incoming
waste streams and provide benefits to the community through product reuse
(bicycles).
* Enhanced residents’ abilities to donate usable goods such as furniture, cabinets,
tiles, and more through a partnership with Habitat for Humanity of Long Island.
Recycling
® Successfully organized and ran 13 electronic waste/paper shredding/drug take-
back events throughout the Town, with over 5,500 residents in attendance,
160,000 pounds of paper shredded, and 80,000 pounds of e-waste recycled.
* Removed over 206,000 pounds of hazardous electronic waste from the solid
Waste stream.
® Prevented over 12,000 gallons of hazardous liquid and 24,000 pounds of
household hazardous waste from polluting the waste stream through the STOP
program.
265

276.text:
e Collected over 30,000 gallons of waste oil through our waste oil collection
program, a portion of which was used to supplement the heating of the
Administrative Building at the landfill.

e Dual stream recycling has proven effective as the Town now produces clean,
marketable products.

* Relocated a satellite glass location in Setauket, and collected 1,136,000 Ibs. of
residential glass at 15 satellite locations throughout the Town. This program
enables the Town to recycle glass that is used in drainage and other applications
at the Solid Waste Management Facility. The Town continues to explore
opportunities to re-incorporate glass into the curbside collection program.

« Provided residents access to paint recycling as part of the New York State Paint
Stewardship Program, recycling approximately 50,000 gallons.

« Worked with 180 multi-family residential complexes for recycling efforts and
bringing into compliance to implement successful recycling programs for their
residents.

» Enhanced residents’ abilities to extend the lifespan of their bicycles by
partnering with the Long Island Bicycle Co-op.

« Continue to collaborate and with regional groups, private vendors and Material
Recovery Facility operators to determine potentials of adding glass back into the
comingle collection.

* Worked with the Town of Smithtown to provide recycling of thin film plastics to
Town residents with two convenient drop-off locations at Brookhaven Town Hall
and the Solid Waste Management Facility in Brookhaven.

Brookhaven Refuse and Recycling District

« Amend the Brookhaven Refuse and Recycling District (now BRRD Il) to extend
service to Strathmore Court Coram development adding 440 households to the
district and revise the term “benefit use tax” to “user fee.”

* Extended 2 collection contracts into extension year. Awarded six (6) new
contracts to provide continued service to the curbside collection districts.

* Design and obtain competitive pricing for an isolation building to be constructed
adjacent to the Transfer Station. This will provide a safe place to identify and
isolate pass thru medical isotopes that come in thru the curbside collection
program so they can be managed in accordance with regulations.

Sustainability

« The “Brew to Moo” program has diverted over 48,000 pounds of spent grains and
organic food scraps produced by local brewers and Town Hall from entering the
waste stream in the past 12 months. This organic material was delivered to local
farms to feed animals.

« Continued food waste composting project at Town Hall. Food waste is collected
at Town Hall offices and its contracted cafeteria vendor and deposited in
composting bins on site to be turned into a beneficial soil amendment. Material
is collected by the Town Staff with the “Brew to Moo” program.

e Provided over 2,300 tons of free compost and mulch for residents at eight Town
locations and restored several properties that were demolished by the Town with
over 750 tons of mulch.

266

277.text:
® Reeycled more than 59,400 pounds of shell collected through the “Half Shells for
Habitat” shell collection program by Seatuck Environmental Association since
program inception (beneficial use that improves waber quality in Moriches Bay).
Worked with Seatuck Environmental Association to improve and expand the
current area of oyster shell recycling to allow for the recycling of oysters from
the Village of Port Jefferson while maintaining compliance with regulations.

» Continued operation of a rooftop mounted solar array which was installed on the
DRSMM Administrative Building and Mechanic's Shop at the landfill.

« Completed construction of a 23-acre Community Solar array system on the closed
portion of the Landfill.

e Completed construction of a 5-acre Solar Array System on the inactive landfill at
Holtsville Ecology Center and began design work for an additional 5-acre area of
solar at the facility.

« Began construction on an expansion of solar resources by at the Manorville
Compost Facility.

« Developed the first RSMM Poster Contest for schools, to promote waste reduction
and recycling.

Quality of Life

« Demolished 12 blighted abandoned houses.

« Removed thousands of illegal signs from public rights-of-way areas.

« Issued 160 summonses for code violations (unregistered vehicles and/or litter
and high grass wiolations).

« Sanitation Inspectors responded to nearly 4,000 private property litter
complaints and over 800 residential high grass complaints.

« Roadside litter crews responded to over 800 roadside litter complaints and 26 in
need of heavy equipment.

e Organized and sponsored the 18th Annual “Great Brookhaven Cleanup,” a Keep
Brookhaven Beautiful anti-litter campaign. This milestone event took place with
nearly 2,000 participants and resulted in 81 tons of litter / debris collected.

« Continue to monitor camera system to identify illegal dumping of wastes on Town
wetlands, rights of way, and within parks properties.

s Successful prosecution of several individuals found to be illegally dumping of
wastes within the Town.

Landfill Operations

« Completed work on a 23.4-acre synthetic cap closure project that will limit the
need for use of natural soil resources. This cap will reduce both leachate quantity
and improve odor control and collection operations. New Cap design has reduced
the labor associated with turf maintenance.

e Initiated design on the next 26-acre synthetic cap closure project that will
reduce the area of open landfill. The permit application will be submitted in the
third quarter of 2026, with construction estimated to begin in the second quarter
of 2027. The new cap design will reduce odor, leachate and labor associated with
turf maintenance.

* Employed the fix before failure maintenance methodology, allowing for better
uptime and availability of the landfill leachate infrastructure.

« Continued our partnership with Stony Brook University to study new methods to
treat landfill gas, recycle ash and improve recycling.

267

278.text:
* Continued work on a Suffolk County Regional Solid Waste Management study in
cooperation with the County and other County municipalities to review and
